title: Veteran pitcher Choi Dong-hwan released by KT after failed comeback attempt - CHOSUNBIZ
text:
Veteran pitcher Choi Dong-hwan released by KT after failed comeback attempt - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 10월 22일(목) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Veteran pitcher Choi Dong-hwan released by KT after failed comeback attempt 
 입력 2026.10.22. 15:50 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 Even Kang Cheol-maejik ultimately could not save "that pitcher."
 The professional baseball team KT Wiz officially announced on the afternoon of the 22nd that it would not renew contracts with 10 players. The players are Choi Dong-hwan, Cho Yi-hyun, Lee Hyun-min, Lee Jun-myung, Kwon Hyo-joon, Kim Min-sung, Jung Jung-woo, Kim Kyu-han, Park Chi-sung, and Choi Dong-hee, among 10 players.
 The most notable player is 37-year-old veteran pitcher Choi Dong-hwan. A graduate of Gyeongdong High School, Choi Dong-hwan was selected by the LG Twins in the 2009 rookie draft, second stage, second round, 13th overall. He spent as many as 16 years with LG, leaving a first-team career record of 344 games, 10 wins, 6 losses, 4 saves, 16 holds and an earned run average of 5.11 (368⅓ innings, 209 earned runs). After a disappointing 2024 season with 26 games, no wins, 1 loss, 2 holds and a 6.95 earned run average, he suffered the pain of being released.
 Choi Dong-hwan was classified as a released player during LG's roster adjustment process on Oct. 7, 2024. The player himself asked the club to release him in order to gain more playing opportunities, and after wavering between extending his career and retirement, he found a new home in KT two months later. Under manager Lee Kang-cheol, the "pitcher trainer," KT had often helped released pitchers stage comebacks with his exceptional insight and leadership.
 Upon his transfer, Choi Dong-hwan went to the first-team spring camps set up in Geelong, Australia and Okinawa, Japan to prepare for the 2025 season. Receiving systematic coaching from manager Lee Kang-cheol and pitching coach Je Chun-mo, he identified the causes of his previous season's slump and pitched well in three exhibition games with a 0.00 earned run average (three scoreless innings), raising expectations for a comeback.
 But the expectations lasted only that long. He wavered with an 8.68 earned run average in his first year with 20 games, 1 win and 1 loss, and this year he disappeared entirely from the first team. He also struggled in the Futures League with 36 games, 3 wins, 1 loss, 7 holds and a 6.11 earned run average, failing to get a call from manager Lee Kang-cheol. From the season opener on March 28 until Oct. 12, he spent 199 days in the second team.
 Cho Yi-hyun (31) also put a period on a long 13-year professional career. After stints with Hanwha Eagles, SK Wyverns and SSG Landers, she joined KT and at one time became a success story of a released player making a comeback, but after three appearances in 2025 and failing to appear on the first-team mound this year, she ended up unemployed. Her first-team career record is 116 games, 10 wins, 18 losses, 1 save, 1 hold and a 6.29 earned run average.
 Meanwhile, regular-season first-place KT will face the playoff winner in game 1 of the Korean Series at Suwon KT Wiz Park on the 2nd of next month.
